new_sources.summary: Abstract Philip Massinger (1583-1640) was probably educated at Salisbury Grammar School, and attended St Alban Hall Oxford in 1602-3, forced to leave when his father died. In 1613 he is next heard of collaborating on plays written for Henslowe. From 1616 to 1625 he wrote many plays together with John Fletcher, principal dramatist for the King’ s Men, becoming their chief dramatist from Fletcher’ s death until 1640, writing for both the Globe and Black friars theatres. Massinger is know to have written all or part of fifty-five plays, twenty-two of which are lost; of the remaining thirty-three, fifteen were his own work.
